theme: कर्म का शुद्धि से योग: निष्कामता, साक्षीभाव, और आत्म-नियंत्रण। / Action purified by yoga: detachment, witness-consciousness, and inner freedom.
context: Arjuna is still weighing renunciation against action. Krishna answers that liberation is not reached by merely giving up activity or by a passive withdrawal from life. A person is truly yogic when the mind is purified, the ego is reduced, and action is done without possessive attachment to result.
contextHindi: अर्जुन अभी भी संन्यास और कर्म के बीच उलझन में हैं। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि मुक्ति केवल कर्म छोड़ देने से नहीं मिलती, न केवल निष्क्रियता से। वह व्यक्ति सच्चा योगी है, जिसका मन शुद्ध हो, अहंकार कम हो, और कर्म परिणाम पर आसक्ति के बिना हो।
sanskritDevanagari:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः |
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ||५-७||
transliteration:
yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ .
sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate ||5-7||

wordByWord.meaning: established in yoga; living in inner harmony, not in agitation.
one whose self is purified; the mind is clear of greed, anger, and egoic distortion.
self-conquered; one who has won mastery over inner impulses and emotional reactivity.
one whose senses are disciplined; not enslaved to sensory craving.
the self is felt as the Self in all beings; a broad, non-separating awareness.

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में कृष्ण ने आत्म-युक्त जीवन का स्वरूप बताया है। योगयुक्त का अर्थ है, ऐसी स्थिति जहाँ मन, बुद्धि और इन्द्रियाँ कर्म करते हुए भी आत्मा को अपने भीतर स्थिर रखती हैं। विशुद्धात्मा वह है जिसके मन में राग-द्वेष की धूल साफ़ हो चुकी है। विजितात्मा वह है जिसने अपने भीतर के चंचल भावों को रोका है, और जितेन्द्रिय वह है जो इन्द्रियों को अपने लिए नहीं, बल्कि आत्म-दर्शन के लिए रखता है। इसलिए कर्म करता हुआ भी साधक लिप्त नहीं होता। वह हर कर्म को ‘मैं कर रहा हूँ’ की भावना से नहीं, ‘अहंकार के बिना, आत्मा के लिए’ इस दृष्टि से करता है। यह पथ न तो निष्क्रियता है, न केवल विचारों की शांति है; यह है कर्म का शुद्धीकरण। अगर हम अपने कर्तृत्व को कम करके, परिणाम को सेवा या अर्पण के रूप में छोड़ दें, तो मन की ऊँचाई बढ़ती है। यही योग का तात्पर्य है—कर्म को रोकना नहीं, उसे अपनेपन से मुक्त करना।
clearEnglish: The verse defines the yogi not by inactivity but by a stable inner center. A person united with yoga is not someone who stops moving; rather, the mind is purified, the ego is less active, and the senses are no longer possessed by craving. The terms viśuddhātmā, vijitātmā, and jitendriyaḥ describe a person whose inner life has become disciplined and inwardly clear. In ordinary experience, action creates bondage because we treat doership and outcome as personal identity. Krishna points to a different stance: the yogi performs tasks without claiming them as a private possession or a source of self-definition. This is not passivity. It is responsibility without ego. In practical terms, a worker can work, a student can study, and a caregiver can care, while refusing to build a drama around results. TEXT: the verse states that a person of purified mind and mastered senses remains untained by action. INFERENCE: freedom grows when agency is loosened and attention shifts from “I did it” to “I acted, without owning the outcome.”

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse plainly says that one whose mind is purified, self-conquered, and sense-controlled acts without being tainted by action.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The DLS summary supports the idea that the real renunciation is not laziness or withdrawal from duty, but surrender of ego and desire. It emphasizes that action remains, while attachment to the self as doer is reduced.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The practical conclusion is that ethical action becomes liberating when it is offered without personal ownership, reputation, or result-attachment.

practicalApplication.label: Work without ego
practicalApplication.text: At the start of a task, pause for three breaths and mentally note: 'I am using body, mind, and skills; I am not claiming the result as my private possession.'

practicalApplication.label: Quiet the inner owner
practicalApplication.text: When a conversation or decision triggers irritability, ask: 'Am I acting from responsibility or from the urge to be seen, praised, or in control?'

reflectionQuestion: When you act with effort but without claiming ownership of the outcome, how does your inner state change under stress?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब आप प्रयास करते हुए भी परिणाम पर स्वामित्व का दावा नहीं करते, तो दबाव में आपकी आंतरिक स्थिति कैसे बदलती है?
